title: Scalar Interpolation: A Better Balance between Vector and Scalar Execution for SuperScalar Architectures
problem: Most compilers vectorize all loop iterations, but processors with distinct scalar and vector execution pipelines remain underutilized. Vectorization forces scalar operations to use vector registers, incurring data movement overhead.
motivation: SuperScalar processors have separate scalar and vector pipelines; better utilization of both pipelines can improve overall performance by balancing workload distribution.
method: Modern processors have separate execution pipelines for vector operations (processing multiple data items together) and scalar operations (processing one at a time). Current compilers typically vectorize entire loops, forcing all operations through the vector pipeline and leaving the scalar pipeline underused. Scalar Interpolation runs some loop iterations on the scalar pipeline and others on the vector pipeline, avoiding the data movement overhead of forcing scalar operations into vector registers. The technique uses either a cost model or runtime testing to determine the optimal ratio of scalar to vectorized iterations.
key_novelty: The first technique to balance scalar and vector pipeline utilization by inserting scalar-only iterations into vectorized loops.
contributions: Scalar interpolation technique for balanced pipeline utilization
Static cost model for interpolation factor selection
Auto-tuning approach for dynamic sweet-spot discovery
limitations: Applicability to compilers other than LLVM not discussed; memory-intensive workload suitability unclear.
